age.evidence: Male Long Evans rats were used in all experiments (source: Charles River Laboratories). Age not stated.

sex.evidence: Male Long Evans rats were used in all experiments

dosing.doses_raw: Psilocybin doses 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10 mg/kg (observation); 0.025-0.1 mg/kg (PR); 0.05-0.1 mg/kg (5-CSRTT standard); 0.01, 0.05, 0.1 mg/kg (5-CSRTT extended ITI)
dosing.evidence: Psilocybin ... was suspended in 0.9% saline and sonicated until fully dissolved. Drug was administered in a volume of 1 ml/kg, subcutaneous (SC) route.

dosing.doses_raw: Ketamine doses 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 60 mg/kg (observation); 0.3-6 mg/kg (PR and 5-CSRTT standard); 1-6 mg/kg (5-CSRTT extended ITI)
dosing.evidence: (±) Ketamine hydrochloride ... was suspended in 0.9% saline and administered at a volume of 1 ml/kg, via the intraperitoneal (IP) route.

handling.evidence: No handling protocol described in Methods.

group_housing.evidence: All study animals were singly housed in a vivarium under a 12 h light:dark cycle

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12 h light:dark cycle (lights on: 06:00 h -18:00 h). All behavioral testing was during the light phase.

assays.assay_name: Spontaneous Locomotor Activity and Behavioural Stereotypy Observation
assays.assay_description: Rats placed immediately post-injection in automated activity chambers (17"x17"x12", Med Associates) for 2 h. Distance traveled, rearing, and ambulatory episodes recorded automatically; technicians scored drug-specific behaviours (head weaving, circling, ataxia, body sway for ketamine; WDS, BMC, YPG, FPT, HLA for psilocybin) every 5 min.

application_type.evidence: Ketamine IP; Psilocybin SC (separate cohorts/experiments within this assay)

setup_habituation.evidence: No apparatus habituation prior to test described.

setup_restrain.evidence: subjects were placed in automated activity test chambers ... for 2 h

food_restriction.evidence: Rats utilized for the overt behavioral experiments had ad-lib access to food and water [in home cage]; no food in activity chambers.

water_restriction.evidence: Ad lib access to water in home cage; no water in activity chambers during 2 h test.

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately post-dose, the subjects were placed in automated activity test chambers ... for 2 h

sample_size.evidence: A total of 30 male Long Evans rats were used for these experiments (N = 15 Ketamine study; N = 15 psilocybin study)

outcomes.summary: Ketamine produced a dose-dependent increase in locomotion and stereotypies (circling, ataxia) with threshold of 10 mg/kg. Psilocybin dose-dependently increased 5-HT2A-mediated behaviours (WDS/BMC) with threshold of 0.3 mg/kg, modestly increased distance traveled at 0.1-0.3 mg/kg, and decreased rearing at 10 mg/kg. Psilocybin-induced WDS/BMC was blocked by 5-HT2A antagonist M100907.
outcomes.statistics: Distance traveled: F6,84=4.4, p<0.01; Rearing: F6,84=6.2, p<0.01; M100907/psilo vs Veh/psilo WDS: p<0.001
outcomes.evidence: Ketamine produced a dose related increase in the incidence of overt behaviors and locomotion with a threshold dose of 10 mg/kg ... Psilocybin (0.03-10 mg/kg) produced a dose related increase in the incidence of behaviors presumed to be 5-HT2A receptor mediated (i.e. WDS/BMC) with a threshold dose of 0.3 mg/kg

B1_num_measures.evidence: distance traveled, rearing, ambulatory episodes, WDS, BMC, YPG, FPT, HLA (and for ketamine: head weaving, circling, ataxia, body sway)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Data reported as totals over 2 h session; no within-session time-course analysis.

B4_ethological.evidence: WDS, BMC, yawning, penile grooming, forepaw treading, hindlimb abduction scored as distinct natural acts

B6_cognitive.evidence: Spontaneous behaviour observation; no learning component.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med Associates activity chambers (beam-break/position tracking); ethological behaviours scored manually by technicians.

E1_environment_type.evidence: automated activity test chambers (17" Wx17" L × 12" H; Med Associates)

E3_bedding.evidence: Standard activity chamber floor; no bedding described.

D1_continuity.evidence: Single 2 h recording per dose; doses given on separate days every 4-5 days.

D2_session_duration.evidence: subjects were placed in automated activity test chambers ... for 2 h

D3_recording_days.evidence: Rats were dosed in a semi-random sequence with test drug or vehicle control every 4-5 days (multiple doses tested per animal)

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline session reported for this assay.

assays.assay_description: Operant chambers (25 × 30 cm, Med Associates) where food-restricted rats lever-press for 45 mg food pellets under a progressive ratio schedule. Break point (failure to earn pellet in 20 min), total lever presses, and session duration measured. Ketamine 0.3-6 mg/kg IP and psilocybin 0.025-0.1 mg/kg SC tested in same cohort under Latin square design; analyses performed in full cohort and 'low responder' tertile.

application_type.evidence: Ketamine IP (0.3-6 mg/kg); Psilocybin SC (0.025-0.1 mg/kg) tested in same task

setup_habituation.evidence: Training phase described but no specific pre-test apparatus habituation.

setup_restrain.evidence: Operant chamber; rats free to move.

food_restriction.evidence: Rats utilized for the 5-choice and progressive ratio experiments were placed on a restricted diet regimen throughout training and testing, where they were fed once a day with approximately 18-20 g of standard laboratory chow at the completion of testing procedures

water_restriction.evidence: Ad lib water in home cage; restriction not described for PR rats.

time_to_assay.evidence: Pretreatment times for psilocybin, ketamine and dizocilpine was 10 min

sample_size.evidence: A total of 72 rats were trained ... effect of ketamine (0.3-6 mg/kg IP; N=68 rats) and psilocybin (0.025-0.1 mg/kg SC; N=72 rats); low responders (N=23 ketamine study; N=24 psilocybin study)

outcomes.summary: In the full cohort, neither drug significantly increased break point overall (ketamine 6 mg/kg actually decreased it). In the 'low responder' tertile, ketamine 1-3 mg/kg and psilocybin 0.05-0.1 mg/kg significantly increased break point and lever presses, suggesting enhanced motivation. Low and high responders did not differ in free-feeding, locomotion, or body weight.
outcomes.statistics: Low responders ketamine: lever press F4,88=6.6, p<0.01; break point F4,88=8.9, p<0.01; session duration F4,88=5.0, p=0.01. Low responders psilocybin: lever press F3,69=4.9, p<0.01; break point F3,69=5.6, p<0.01.
outcomes.evidence: ketamine 1-3 mg/kg doses to increase each measure relative to vehicle pretreatment ... increases in both measures following psilocybin 0.05-0.1 mg/kg pretreatment relative to vehicle [in low responders]

B1_num_measures.evidence: Recorded measures included break point (number of pellets earned), total lever presses made during the test session, and test session duration

B6_cognitive.evidence: Operant progressive ratio schedule requires learned lever-press contingency.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med PC software (lever-press event detection, not behavioural classification).

E6_spatial.evidence: Single aluminum enclosure (25×30 cm) with lever and hopper.

E8_food_water.evidence: lever press for a food reward (45 mg Bioserv pellets) delivered during the session

D1_continuity.evidence: each animal received each treatment over repeated test sessions with 3-4 days intervals; baseline measured over 5-7 days

D2_session_duration.evidence: session duration ~15-19 min reported (e.g., Veh: 15.1 ± 2.0 min; Psilo 0.1 mg/kg: 18.7 ± 2.5 min); break point determined when rat failed to earn pellet in 20 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Latin square with 4-5 doses per drug × 3-4 day intervals plus 5-7 day baseline pretest; both drugs tested in same cohort; total recording days for this assay exceed 7.

D4_baseline.evidence: Subjects were also ranked based on pellets earned and total lever presses over a 7-days pretest period

assays.assay_description: Operant chambers (Med Associates) with array of five nose-poke niches and food magazine. Food-restricted rats respond to brief light cue (SD 0.75 s or 0.3 s) after ITI (5 s standard, 10 s extended). Measures: %correct, %hit, omissions, premature responses (PREM), perseverative responses (PSV), correct latency, magazine latency, total trials. Session up to 100 trials or 60 min. Ketamine 0.3-6 mg/kg IP and psilocybin 0.01-0.1 mg/kg SC tested across standard and extended-ITI conditions; analyses in full cohort and low/high performer or low/high impulsive tertiles.

setup_habituation.evidence: Training described but no separate pre-test habituation specified.

setup_restrain.evidence: Operant chamber; rats free to move.

food_restriction.evidence: Rats utilized for the 5-choice and progressive ratio experiments were placed on a restricted diet regimen throughout training and testing

water_restriction.evidence: Ad lib water in home cage; restriction not described.

time_to_assay.evidence: Pretreatment times for psilocybin, ketamine and dizocilpine was 10 min

sample_size.evidence: Ketamine standard N=36; Psilocybin standard N=24; Ketamine extended ITI N=24; Psilocybin extended ITI N=57. Subgroup tertiles N=8-19.

outcomes.summary: Under standard conditions, ketamine 6 mg/kg reduced %hit and increased omissions/premature responses; lower doses had no overall effect, but in low-performer subgroup ketamine 1-3 mg/kg and psilocybin 0.05-0.1 mg/kg modestly improved %hit (attentional accuracy). Under extended ITI, dizocilpine produced large increases in PREM/PSV; ketamine and psilocybin produced more modest increases in PREM/PSV restricted to low-impulsive subgroups, with no effect on accuracy.
outcomes.statistics: Ketamine 6 mg/kg overall: F4,140>5.1, p<0.01 on %hit, omissions, PREM, PSV. Low performers ketamine: %hit F4,44=3.9, p<0.01. Low performers psilocybin: %hit F2,14=4.8, p=0.02. Extended ITI ketamine LI subgroup: treatment×subgroup PREM F3,42=4.2, p=0.01; PSV F3,42=4.1, p=0.01. Extended ITI psilocybin LI: PREM F3,54=3.4, p=0.02; PSV F3,54=3.0, p=0.04.
outcomes.evidence: ketamine (1-3 mg/kg) increased PREM responses in the LI group ... psilocybin significantly increased PREM and PSV responses at the 0.05-0.1 mg/kg doses relative to vehicle pretreatment [in LI group]; small improvement in accuracy at 1 mg/kg and 3 mg/kg compared to vehicle pretreatment on % hit measure

B1_num_measures.evidence: #Correct, #Incorrect, #Missed, %Correct, %Hit, PREM, PSV, correct latency, magazine latency, total trials

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Session totals only; no within-session time-course.

B4_ethological.evidence: Operant nose-pokes and latencies, not ethological behaviour.

B6_cognitive.evidence: 5-CSRTT measures attention and response control; learned stimulus-response task.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med PC software with niche/magazine photocells (event detection).

B8_multivariate.evidence: Univariate ANOVAs with subgroup tertile analyses; no PCA/multivariate.

E6_spatial.evidence: Array of five square niches (2.5×2.5×2.5 cm) on a curved panel, plus a reward magazine on the opposite wall — physically distinct compartments.

E8_food_water.evidence: delivery of a food pellet (45 mg food pellet, Bioserv)

D1_continuity.evidence: drug testing began ... animals tested twice weekly ... run under baseline conditions over intervening days; Latin square repeated measures design

D2_session_duration.evidence: Each session ran for either 100 trials or 60 min, whichever endpoint was achieved first

D3_recording_days.evidence: 5-day baseline subgrouping window plus Latin-square testing across 4-5 doses twice weekly under two test conditions (standard + extended ITI) — recording across well over 7 days for this assay.

D4_baseline.evidence: Subgrouping made in this experiment based on baseline % correct made over 5 days preceding these experiments

judge_notes: Three distinct behavioural assays retained: (1) 2-h spontaneous activity/stereotypy observation (combining locomotion and observer-scored ethological signs — these were measured in the same recording session and constitute one assay), (2) Progressive Ratio operant task, (3) 5-CSRTT (collapsing standard 5 s ITI and extended 10 s ITI conditions into one assay per rubric guidance that different stimulus parameters of the same paradigm = one assay).
PK/LC-MS quantification and plasma sampling are physiological/analytical endpoints, not behavioural assays — excluded.

B1 for the activity/observation assay scored 7+ because the paper reports distance, rearing, ambulatory episodes, and multiple separately scored ethological behaviours (WDS, BMC, YPG, FPT, HLA, plus for ketamine head weaving, circling, ataxia, body sway).
E6 for 5-CSRTT scored 1 (multiple zones) following glm — the five niches plus magazine on the opposing wall constitute physically distinct compartments; qwen/gptoss under-scored this.

D3 raised to 8-14 for PR and 5-CSRTT given the Latin-square design with multiple doses tested per animal at 3-4 day intervals plus 5-7 day baseline periods — total recording days for these assays clearly exceed 7.
Food restriction: 'before' for PR and 5-CSRTT (restricted diet regimen throughout training/testing per Methods); 'during' for activity test (ad lib in home cage, no food in chamber).
Group housing scored 'no' — paper explicitly states all animals were singly housed.
Day/night flipped scored 'no' — standard light cycle (lights on 06:00-18:00) with testing in light phase explicitly stated.
